lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: The contact details look like placeholders if they are literal, and the profile link may be inactive.
items.because: A résumé should provide usable professional contact information.

items.says: The date of birth does not belong on most private-sector résumés.
items.because: It is irrelevant to qualifications and unnecessarily shares personal information.

items.says: Nationality does not belong on most private-sector résumés.
items.because: It is generally unnecessary and should not be used to imply work authorization.

items.says: The bond purchase does not explain how it hedged interest-rate risk.
items.because: Buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration could increase exposure, depending on the balance sheet.

items.says: Clarify which periods or application groups the approval rates compare.
items.because: The comparison basis is not stated.

items.says: Explain how you know early defaults did not rise.
items.because: The basis for that result is not given.

items.says: Clarify your role in changing the thresholds and producing the results.
items.because: The wording implies a direct link between your findings and the results.

items.says: “Writes” uses the wrong tense for a completed role.
items.because: It conflicts with the dated experience entry.

items.says: Clarify the annual comparison period for missed covenant tests.
items.because: The reduction is given as a yearly figure.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the checklist.
items.because: The wording should accurately reflect your contribution.

items.says: Clarify whether the time reduction was per memo.
items.because: The scope of the saving should be clear.

items.says: Clarify whether you built the template yourself or contributed to it.
items.because: The scope of your ownership is not specified.

items.says: Explain what the USD 600M figure represents.
items.because: The company scale measure is unclear.

items.says: Define the forecast-error measure and its period.
items.because: “Under 4%” does not say what was measured or when.

items.says: Check the claimed connection between the forecast and the early debt paydown.
items.because: The connection should remain only if the forecast genuinely informed treasury’s decision.

items.says: Clarify the scope of the 30 automated reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
items.because: It is unclear whether the reconciliations were the full set or a subset.

items.says: Clarify what you personally did to shorten the close.
items.because: Your contribution is not specified.

items.says: Clarify your part in modeling the capital plan.
items.because: Your individual contribution is unclear.

items.says: Explain which assumptions were standardized and whether they were company-approved.
items.because: Using the same discount rate for every request could raise questions when project risks differ.

items.says: “Mapping” uses the wrong tense for a completed role.
items.because: It conflicts with the dated experience entry.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the mapping and allocation-rule changes.
items.because: The scope of your contribution is unclear.

items.says: Tie the reduction in manual entries to the same process and period as the prior-close testing.
items.because: The basis for connecting the testing and result is unclear.

items.says: Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC is a valuation mismatch.
items.because: FCFE is ordinarily discounted at the cost of equity, while WACC is ordinarily used with free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: Include a substantiated operational outcome for the training if one is available.
items.because: The bullet states the activity and number trained but no operational result.

items.says: Give the valuation date and explain the comparison with market price.
items.because: What “within 6% of the market price” means is unclear.

items.says: Explain the purpose and assumptions behind the market-price comparison.
items.because: Landing close to market price does not, on its own, show that the valuation was accurate.

items.says: The stated 25% drop from USD 50 to USD 40 is incorrect.
items.because: The decrease is 20% of the USD 50 starting value.

items.says: Specify what a one-point rise in the discount rate means.
items.because: The sensitivity input is unclear.

items.says: Check that the sensitivity describes the model output accurately.
items.because: The stated result needs to match what the model shows.

items.says: Substantiate or remove the measured forecast-accuracy improvement.
items.because: The metric, comparison, and check against actual outcomes are unclear for a ten-year forecast.

items.says: Clarify the FP&A team’s relationship to the student investment fund and your role.
items.because: “FP&A team” may be confusing or describe a separate activity.

items.says: Replace the generic description with the reporting and analysis you actually performed.
items.because: The bullet does not identify the fund work.

items.says: Clarify what performance the report covered.
items.because: The scope of the benchmark comparison is not specified.

items.says: The tools list is very short.
items.because: It names only Excel.

items.says: Specify Excel capabilities you can substantiate if it is your only relevant tool.
items.because: The entry otherwise gives little detail about your proficiency.

items.says: Make the broad methods list reflect the role you want.
items.because: FP&A, corporate finance, and credit analysis call for different emphasis.

items.says: Give the most relevant experience greater prominence for the target role.
items.because: Manufacturing work is most relevant to FP&A, while the bank experience merits more emphasis for credit analysis.
